summary: Weekly POC sync to review evaluation results across candidate models, decide on version-pinning strategy and fallback policy. Agreement to run larger latency/throughput benchmarks and validate quantized model accuracy on Orion's prompt set. Action items assigned: benchmarking, pricing, and prompt set delivery.
transcript: Header: 2027-01-26 10:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (Orion Head of ML), Ravi (Orion Platform Eng), Tom (Orion PM)
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Short agenda - review the evals you sent last week, discuss pinning strategy, and next steps for benchmarks and VPC testing.

[00:15] Lena: Cool, yeah thanks. We pushed a small eval yesterday - 200 prompts mostly shopping cart edge cases, personalization snippets. Quick note, some transcription in the doc had a couple typos, we fixed them.

[00:34] Diego: Got them, I ran the baseline comparison against redwood-model-v1-9 and v2-3 small-quant. Initial accuracy delta is about 2.8% on your rubric, with v2-3 showing slightly more hallucination on SKU normalization prompts.
[00:52] Ravi: When you say hallucination, can you give an example? That's a blocker for our returns flow.

[01:05] Diego: Sure - for example prompt asking to map a free-text SKU like 'red short sleeve tee, size L' to canonical SKU, v2-3 sometimes invents sizes when metadata absent. v1-9 tends to be more conservative but slower and more costly per token.
[01:26] Tom: So tradeoff is latency/cost vs correctness. Our priority list is: correctness for checkout flows, then latency for search suggestions. Is that how Redwood is seeing it also?

[01:45] Maya: Yup, exactly. We recommend pinning the checkout-related routes to v1-9 for now, and routing less-critical suggestion routes to v2-3 small-quant. That gives you cost savings while protecting critical paths.
[02:10] Lena: Sounds reasonable. How do rollbacks look? If v2-3 pushes a bad change, do we have automatic fallback?

[02:23] Diego: Yes - we can configure per-route fallback to the pinned version or to a higher-tier model. Redwood's runtime supports immediate fallbacks if error rate or quality regressions exceed thresholds. We usually run a canary for 5-10% traffic for 24h before full rollout.
[02:45] Ravi: Any specifics on metrics to trigger fallback? We want something objective, not just eyeballing.

[02:55] Diego: We can do combined signals: latency tail (p95 > target), error rate (HTTP 5xx), and quality regressions measured by your eval suite hitting a delta (e.g., >3% drop in exact-match). We'll wire synthetic checks too.
[03:20] Lena: That makes sense. On the quantized model, we're concerned about token-level regressions - can you run a more robust eval (bleu/chrF or our rubric) at 1k samples?

[03:36] Maya: Diego, can you take that as a deliverable? Run 1k-sample accuracy + latency/throughput benchmark across v1-9 (fp16), v2-3 (small-quant), and v2-3 (fp16) so we can see overheads and QA tradeoffs.
[03:55] Diego: Yep - I'll stand that up on a cluster, it'll include both single-request latency and batch throughput profiles. I'll include raw logs and a summary table.
[04:12] Tom: Also, how does prefix/KV caching factor in? For suggestion routes we could leverage caching to get latency down further.
[04:24] Diego: Good call. For suggestion routes, caching common prefixes and using batching can dramatically reduce cost; I'll include a simulated prefix cache run in the benchmark.
[04:41] Ravi: On the infra side, we need to test VPC peering and private deployment creds. We have a maintenance window next week - can Redwood do a private deploy smoke test then?
[04:55] Maya: Yes, we can. We will need the peering subnet details and an account for the test. Ravi, can you confirm a 2-hour window and share the network ranges by EOD Monday?
[05:12] Ravi: I can confirm by Monday. Also need to understand KMS integration, we use HashiCorp Vault - will Redwood's private use our KMS or integrate with HSM?
[05:25] Diego: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS integrations, including Vault. We can provide the integration guide; Maya will share the doc.
[05:40] Lena: Back to pinning - what's the recommended config format? We want a per-route manifest and the ability to change pin with a single API call.

[05:51] Maya: We'll send the pinning manifest example. It's a small JSON doc you can store in config git: route -> model_version -> fallback_policy. Changing the pin is an atomic operation and supports rollout percentages.
[06:08] Tom: Any gotchas around tokenization differences between versions? We noticed small token-count differences earlier which impacted billing.

[06:20] Diego: Tokenization can vary slightly across model versions. We'll include token delta in the benchmark and suggest a billing guardrail: monitor token/unit cost over first 72h of traffic after pin changes.
[06:36] Lena: Good. For acceptance, we might require no more than 1.5% drop in our rubric for suggestion flows and 0% drop for checkout flows. Is that enforceable with automatic rollback?
[06:50] Diego: Yes, set the rule in the rollout. If your evaluation service reports regression beyond threshold or request-level QA fails, the system can auto-fallback and alert your SREs.

[07:05] Maya: I'm going to recap the decisions - we pin checkout routes to redwood-model-v1-9 (fp16), suggestion routes to redwood-model-v2-3-small-quant with a 10% canary for 24h. Diego to run extended benchmarks; Lena to provide 500-1k prompts; Maya to send pricing and pinning manifest; Ravi to confirm VPC peering window.
[07:35] Tom: Quick question on SLAs: if we move to Dedicated, what's the latency SLO and credits? We might be looking at reserved for black Friday.

[07:47] Maya: Dedicated has SLA backed uptime and latency tiers; I'll include the SLA excerpt in the pricing doc. For Black Friday we'd recommend reserved capacity with burst pools - we'll show cost models in the addendum.
[08:03] Lena: Also, can you run a small A/B using our live traffic capture anonymized? We want to see real-world RMSE on ranking features.
[08:15] Diego: We can. For privacy we'll route through a sandbox and scrub PII. We'll need a sanitized dump or a live mirror with redaction.
[08:30] Ravi: I'll coordinate with infra; probably easier to do a small live mirror for a 2-hour window after the benchmark phase.
[08:42] Maya: Great. Any other blockers?
[08:48] Lena: Not from me. Main thing is we want the benchmark and the pinning manifest to review - once we see the 1k-sample results we'll lock the pins for prod canary.
[09:02] Tom: Agreed. Also please include a short rollback runbook in the doc so Eng on-call can follow it quickly.
[09:12] Maya: Will do. I'll include a one-page runbook and a checklist for canary. Diego will share the benchmark results and raw logs.
[09:26] Diego: I'll also surface a few corner cases we saw where quantization impacted certain entity extraction prompts so you can validate.
[09:37] Maya: Ok wrapping up - next sync same time next week unless we schedule before after benchmark. Thanks everyone.
[09:45] Call ended
